evals.prompt: Split this epic into shippable stories: 'Customers can save their cart, return later on any device, and check out with a saved payment method.'
assertions: Every story is demoable to a non-engineer — a story whose demo is 'look at this database table' is re-cut as a vertical slice
Every acceptance criterion is pass/fail without interpretation and written in Gherkin
Acceptance criteria are concrete enough that a tester who has not seen the epic can verdict them
Dependencies between stories are stated, and a recommended build order follows from them
Stories are independently shippable rather than layered horizontally (all backend, then all frontend)

evals.prompt: Turn the shift-swap PRD in prd-shift-swap.md into user stories for next week's planning, with acceptance criteria and the order we should build them in.
assertions: Each story delivers something a nurse or ward manager can use, rather than a layer such as database schema, API endpoints or UI screens
Flags the conflict between 'manager approval is required for all swaps' and section 9.4 of the staff agreement (same-grade, same-ward swaps need only notification), and does not silently pick one
Notices that the PRD's worked example is wrong (40 + 12 hours is 52, which is over the 48-hour limit) and writes acceptance criteria that enforce the 48-hour rule
Any story that needs a change to the payroll export is marked as blocked until the January freeze lifts, not placed in the near-term build order
Acceptance criteria are pass/fail with specific values from the PRD, such as the 48 hours in a rolling 7 days and the grade rule
Does not invent requirements, roles or rules that are not in the PRD, and adds no mobile app stories
Has no more than eight stories

evals.prompt: I coordinate volunteers for our town's food festival. We want our sign-up website to let people sign up for time slots, get reminders, and swap slots with each other. A developer friend said to send him 'user stories'. Can you write them? No more than five, as one short list I can send him.
assertions: Splits the work into pieces a volunteer or coordinator could each try out on their own, with signing up for a slot coming before reminders and swapping
Each story has at least one concrete check for when it is done
Does not invent details the user didn't give, such as reminder channel, timing or slot limits, or marks them clearly as open questions for the developer
Gives a suggested build order with a reason
Has no more than five stories, short enough to send as one list
Delivers the list without first asking questions
